title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Residue Detection on Surfscan SP7
subtitle: Post-Lithography Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP7 system to detect and classify Residue defects during post-lithography inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Residue defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP7 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP7
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Residue
- Process Step: Post-Lithography
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP7 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-lithography monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP7
Software Version: v14.2.894
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_14nm_POST_LITHOGRAPHY
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: High (107 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP7 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Residue defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 56 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.8% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-05-24
Wafers Tested: 31
Total Defects Found: 4343
Defect Density: 614.41 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.1%
Capture Rate: 99.7%
Test Duration: 137 minutes
System Uptime: 97.6%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP7 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Residue at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Residue at 14nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
